owner ruling 2026-08-14: character-only live mid-action state {repairing, position}, documented on the LuaControl base shared by LuaPlayer and character entities (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/classes/LuaControl.html#repair_state). Characters never transfer - EntityScanner.is_exportable_entity rejects type == "character" and Gateway.evacuate_passengers teleports them to Nauvis at the sole source-delete chokepoint - so the carrier is structurally absent from every payload. Measured 2.1.11: the read throws "Entity is not character." on all 39 entity types present on both standing fixtures.

CorpsePrototype.expires defaults true, time_before_removed defaults 120 s and remove_on_entity_placement defaults true (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/prototypes/CorpsePrototype.html) - a corpse is a self-deleting decorative remnant by documented default, not built state. Its subclass gate is its own ("Entity is not corpse.", distinct from "Entity is not character-corpse." measured at 2.1.11), so the shipped character-corpse pair does not cover it, and zero corpse entities exist on either standing fixture.

CombatRobotPrototype.time_to_live is a mandatory field (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/prototypes/CombatRobotPrototype.html#time_to_live) - the robot is temporary by design - and combat_robot_owner is optional with nil legal (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/classes/LuaEntity.html#combat_robot_owner). The referent is a character, which never enters a payload (export scan excludes it, the source-delete chokepoint evacuates it), so the reference is unresolvable by construction and the only reachable destination value is nil.

Corrected 2026-08-16: the prior reason's premise — that no rail or rolling stock is placeable on a space platform — is false for script placement. Measured on host-2 at 2.1.11 on a throwaway platform reading gravity 0, pressure 0, planet nil: surface.create_entity placed straight-rail and cargo-wagon, entity.train then resolved on the wagon and train.manual_mode read true, so a subject does exist by that route. What surface_conditions gates is the player/bot build path: on that same platform surface.can_place_entity returned false for straight-rail and cargo-wagon and true for gate, against prototype conditions gravity >= 1 for both plus pressure <= 300000 for rail (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/classes/LuaSurface.html#can_place_entity). ignore stands on that narrower ground: no player or bot route can place rolling stock on a platform, so no production platform carries a train, and the only subjects are script-placed test rigs. The train handler and its schedule restore remain dormant on this surface class.

Documented as a tie-breaker among entities at the same point (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/classes/LuaEntity.html#pickup_target) - the destination re-derives it from pickup_position, which is itself derived from the direction create_entity already restores. Measured over all 187 inserters on lab-transfer-fixture-v1 at 2.1.11: 175 have a pickup_target whose bounding box covers that inserter own pickup_position, 12 read nil, 0 disagree; and no module code ever assigns it.

Destination travel state is set by the import, not the payload: import-pipeline.lua:222 writes space_location = park_target at platform creation and import-completion.lua re-parks and verifies. Measured 2.1.11: both live platforms read space_connection = nil, speed = 0 while parked, which is the only state a transfer starts from. distance, speed and space_location are all RW and a space_connection write resets distance to 0.5 (https://lua-api.factorio.com/2.1.11/classes/LuaSpacePlatform.html#space_connection), so resume-in-transit stays feasible later as a feature, needing those three together rather than this attribute alone.
